stem:
Anaya holds a bar magnet a short distance above a pile of iron pins. The pins jump up and stick to the magnet before she touches them.

Which claim correctly identifies the force?

options.text: A magnetic force acts on the iron pins without contact.
A magnetic force acts only after the pins already touch the magnet.
Any force that moves the pins must be contact friction from the table alone.
The pins jump because gravity pulls them upward toward the magnet.

teacher.key_rationale: Magnetic force can act at a distance on magnetic materials such as iron pins. Requiring prior contact, blaming only table friction, or swapping in upward gravity miss the non-contact magnetic-force hinge.
